# core


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

[`fetch()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch) reads
URLs with plain HTTP or a browser-backed tier.
[`to_md()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#to_md)
cleans HTML. The module also crawls sites, discovers XHR calls, and
reads YouTube, arXiv, and GitHub sources.

`heavy`, `stealthy`, `session`, or `auto` to select the fetch tier.

[`to_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#to_md)/[`html2md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#html2md)
run readability’s article extractor by default — right for a fetched
page, since it drops nav, ads and furniture. For a document somebody
saved deliberately, pass `readability=False`: it converts the whole
document, minus script/style/noscript/template and comments.

### get_page

``` python
def get_page(
    url, method:str='GET', payload:NoneType=None, heavy:bool=False, stealthy:bool=False, session:bool=False,
    allow_private:NoneType=None, **kw
)->Response:
```

*Fetch `url`. `session=True` (or a port int) drives the persistent debug
Chrome via CDP, reusing its logged-in cookies.*

Every fetch in fossick arrives here, which is why the private-address
check lives here and not in
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch):
[`crawl`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#crawl),
[`replay_xhr`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#replay_xhr),
[`download_files`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#download_files)
and `http_get` would each have to remember.

### fetch

``` python
def fetch(
    url:str, # URL to fetch
    sel:str=None, # CSS selector to extract (None = full page)
    method:str='GET', # HTTP method; 'POST' sends payload as JSON body
    payload:dict=None, # POST body (JSON) or GET query params
    heavy:bool=False, # Full JS rendering via headless browser
    stealthy:bool=False, # Anti-bot stealth fetcher (Cloudflare etc.)
    capture_xhr:bool=False, # Capture XHR calls made by the page (only works with heavy or stealthy)
    session:bool=False, # Route through the persistent debug Chrome (reuses its logged-in cookies); True or a port int
    auto:bool=False, # Auto-escalate plain->heavy->stealthy->session on bot-block detection
    allow_private:bool=None, # Allow localhost/intranet targets (default: refuse; $FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE=1)
    **kw
)->Response: # Extra kwargs passed to scrapling (e.g. verify, headers)
```

*Fetch `url`, return a Response with `.html` (raw or `sel`-extracted),
`.xhr`, `.status`.*

### Bot walls

[`_blocked()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#_blocked)
detects Cloudflare/Anubis-style interstitials. `auto=True` escalates
tiers until one is clean.

``` python
# A site behind Cloudflare: a plain fetch hits the bot wall, and _blocked() flags it for escalation
cf = fetch('https://www.scrapingcourse.com/cloudflare-challenge', verify=False)
assert cf.status == 403, f'expected a Cloudflare 403 challenge, got {cf.status}'
assert _blocked(cf) is True            # fetch(auto=True) escalates from here (heavy -> stealthy -> session)
print('cloudflare:', cf.status, '| blocked?', _blocked(cf))
```

``` python
# A site behind Anubis (proof-of-work bot wall): _blocked() now recognizes it, so fetch(auto=True) escalates
an = fetch('https://anubis.techaro.lol/', verify=False)
assert 'making sure' in an.html.lower(), 'expected the Anubis challenge page'
assert _blocked(an) is True            # Anubis markers are in _BLOCK_MARKERS -> auto escalates past this wall
print('anubis wall detected by _blocked?', _blocked(an))
```

``` python
# regression: a normal page that merely *mentions* captcha must NOT read as a bot wall.
# Wikipedia embeds hCaptcha config keys in its page JS -- the word is there, but there's no challenge widget.
wiki = fetch('https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anubis', verify=False)
assert wiki.status == 200 and 'captcha' in wiki.html.lower()   # the word IS present on the page...
assert _blocked(wiki) is False   # ...but _BLOCK_MARKERS matches captcha *widgets* (g-recaptcha/h-captcha/...), not the word
```

``` python
# fetch(auto=True): walks plain->heavy->stealthy->session, stops at the first unblocked tier, tags .tier
plain = fetch('https://example.com', auto=True, verify=False)
assert plain.status == 200 and plain.tier == 'plain'   # a static page needs no escalation
print('example.com ->', plain.tier)
```

``` python
# browser_session(): open ONE browser, reuse it across fetches (skips per-URL relaunch)
with browser_session() as bf:
    a = bf('https://example.com')
    b = bf('https://httpbin.org/html')
assert a.status == 200 and b.status == 200
assert len(a.html) > 0 and len(b.html) > 0
```

``` python
# fetch(session=True): route through the persistent debug Chrome, reusing its logged-in cookies
pg = fetch('https://httpbin.org/headers', session=True)
assert pg.status == 200
print(pg.html[:200])
```

### get_pdf

``` python
def get_pdf(
    url_or_path:str, # URL or local path to PDF
    save_path:NoneType=None, # optional path to save the PDF (directory or full path)
    **scrapling_kw
)->pdf_oxide.pdf_oxide.PdfDocument | None: # extra kwargs passed to scrapling fetcher (e.g. verify, headers, timeout)
```

*Fetch PDF from URL or path and return as PdfDocument, or None if it is
not a PDF.*

Identity comes from the %PDF- magic bytes, not the URL suffix. arXiv
serves its PDFs from extensionless URLs (`arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03762v7`),
so a suffix check rejected every paper fossick is most used to read.
NCBI PMC’s download page is a proof-of-work interstitial; its challenge
is solved once here rather than mistaken for a failed PDF.

``` python
import tempfile
```

``` python
sp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
```

``` python
sdt = 'https://selfdeterminationtheory.org/SDT/documents/2000_RyanDeci_SDT.pdf'
sdt_p = get_pdf(sdt, save_path=sp, verify=False)
```

``` python
sdt_p.to_markdown_all()[:200]
```

``` python
gdr = 'https://selfdeterminationtheory.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/1997_GrolnickDeciRyan.pdf'
gcr = get_pdf(gdr, save_path=sp, verify=False)
```

``` python
gcr.to_markdown_all()[:200]
```

`title, authors, summary, published, link, pdf_url,* pdf_path` and, with

Only JSON-able fields are cached — a `PdfDocument` is a live handle, not
cache content.

``` python

```

### replay_xhr

``` python
def replay_xhr(
    capture:dict, # a request dict from cdp.calls() or find_xhr(session=True)[i].capture
    data:NoneType=None, # override request body (str/dict); defaults to the captured body
    port:int=9223, # debug Chrome port to pull cookies from
    use_cookies:bool=True, # attach the browser's cookies for this domain (keeps auth)
    **kw
)->Response: # Extra kwargs passed to the underlying Fetcher (headers, params, verify)
```

*Replay a browser-captured request as a fast plain-HTTP call,
authenticated via the debug Chrome’s cookies.*

### find_xhr

``` python
def find_xhr(
    url:str, # URL to visit with browser
    pattern:str='*', # Glob or regex pattern to filter captured XHR URLs
    session:bool=False, # Use the persistent debug Chrome (authenticated) instead of a throwaway browser
    port:int=9223, # debug Chrome port (only when session=True)
    tail:int=3, # seconds to keep listening after navigation (only when session=True)
    **kw
)->list: # Extra kwargs passed to fetch (verify, network_idle, etc.)
```

*Visit `url`, return \[{url, content_type, data, capture}\] for each
XHR/fetch call made. `capture` replays via
[`replay_xhr`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#replay_xhr).*

### compile_pattern

``` python
def compile_pattern(
    pattern
):
```

*Compile pattern as regex; if invalid (e.g. bare glob like* foo*),
convert via fnmatch first*

``` python
assert compile_pattern('.*products.*').search('https://api.example.com/products?q=1')
assert compile_pattern('*products*').search('https://api.example.com/products?q=1')
assert not compile_pattern('*products*').search('https://api.example.com/search')
assert compile_pattern('.*[Ss]earch.*').search('https://api.example.com/Search')
```

### paginate_api

``` python
def paginate_api(
    url:str, # API endpoint URL
    payload:dict=None, # Request body (POST) or params (GET)
    page_field:str='pageNumber', # Payload key to increment for each page
    size_field:str='pageSize', # Payload key for page size (detects last page)
    results_field:str=None, # Response key with items list (auto-detect if None)
    method:str='POST', # HTTP method
    max_pages:int=10, page_size:int=24, # Page size to request (only used if not in payload)
    page_start:int=1, # Starting page number (default 1)
    save:bool=False, # If True, saves each page's items to disk
    save_file:str='{url}_page_{page}.json', # Filepath pattern for saving (only used if save=True)
    force:bool=False, # If True, forces re-fetching even if saved file exists
    **kw
)->list: # Extra kwargs passed to fetch() (verify, headers, etc.)
```

*Paginate through a JSON API, collecting all results. Auto-detects the
items list in response.*

### json_records

``` python
def json_records(
    data, # any decoded JSON payload
    min_len:int=2, # shortest list of dicts worth calling records
    key:str=None, # only accept a list held under this key, at any depth
    with_key:bool=False, # also return the key the records were found under
    max_depth:int=6
):
```

*The longest list of dicts anywhere in `data` — how an API’s records are
found when no key is named.*

A JSON API puts its rows where it likes: at the top level, under
`results`, or under `data.products.items`. Scanning only the top level
finds the first two and silently misses the third, which reads as an
empty response rather than as a payload nobody looked into.

``` python
from fastcore.test import test_eq
```

``` python
_pages = crawl('https://lego.sankalpa.sh/', max_pages=2, verify=False)
assert isinstance(_pages, list), f"Expected list, got {type(_pages)}"
assert len(_pages) > 0, "Expected at least one page"
assert all(p.status == 200 for p in _pages), "Non-200 pages should be skipped"
assert all(len(p.html) > 0 for p in _pages), "html should be non-empty"
assert len({p.url for p in _pages}) == len(_pages), "url values should be unique"
```

``` python
# crawl(reuse=True): a JS-rendered crawl keeps ONE browser open across pages (no per-page relaunch)
_jsp = crawl('https://quotes.toscrape.com/js/', max_pages=2, heavy=True, reuse=True)
assert _jsp and all(p.status == 200 for p in _jsp)
assert all(len(p.html) > 500 for p in _jsp)      # JS actually rendered content into the DOM
```

``` python
# paginate_api: test with JSONPlaceholder (free public REST API, GET-based)
posts = paginate_api(
    'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts',
    payload={'_page': 1, '_limit': 5},
    page_field='_page',
    size_field='_limit',
    method='GET',
    verify=False,
)
assert len(posts) >= 5
assert 'title' in posts[0]
```

`find_xhr(session=True)` uses the authenticated debug Chrome.

``` python
# find_xhr(session=True) -> replay_xhr: capture a request via the authenticated debug Chrome,
# then replay it as a fast plain-HTTP call using the browser's cookies
hits = find_xhr('https://httpbin.org/json', pattern='.*json', session=True)
assert hits, 'no matching request captured'
assert hits[0].capture, 'each hit should carry a replayable capture'
r = replay_xhr(hits[0].capture)
assert r.status == 200
print(hits[0].url, '->', r.status)
```


*Download YouTube media; format=‘audio’|‘video’|yt-dlp format string.
Returns Path to saved file.*

``` python
p = download_yt('https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aircAruvnKk', format='audio', save_dir='/tmp/fossick_test')
assert p.exists(), f"file not found: {p}"
assert p.suffix == '.mp3', f"expected .mp3, got {p.suffix}"
print(f"saved to: {p} ({p.stat().st_size // 1024} KB)")
```

## One door

[`read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#read) accepts
every supported target and returns the same fields: `ok`, `kind`,
`title`, `source`, `text`, `skipped`, and `meta`.
[`what_is`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#what_is)
selects the reader. Local paths take precedence over URL patterns, and
GitHub file URLs take precedence over repository URLs.

This gives collectors and indexes one input contract for web pages,
PDFs, arXiv papers, YouTube videos, GitHub content, and local files.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/core.py#L921"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### read

``` python
def read(
    target:str, # a URL, an arXiv id, a YouTube link, a GitHub repo or file, a PDF, a local path
    sel:str=None, # CSS selector, for the web cases
    auto:bool=True, # escalate plain -> heavy -> stealthy -> logged-in Chrome past bot walls
    pages:bool=False, # PDFs as `[(page_no, text)]` rather than one string
    save_dir:str='.', # where a downloaded PDF is kept
    force:bool=False, # ignore whatever the reader has cached
    **kw
)->AttrDict: # `(ok, kind, title, source, text, skipped, meta)`
```

*Read a supported target and return a common result.*

Read failures set `ok=False` and give the reason in `skipped`.
Directories and GitHub repositories set `meta['path']` and leave `text`
empty.

``` python
# the network cases, which the CI run does not reach
r = read('https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762')
r.ok, r.kind, r.title, r.meta['authors'][:2]
```

``` python
p = read('https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/7181-attention-is-all-you-need.pdf', pages=True)
p.ok, p.kind, len(p.text), p.text[0][0]
```

``` python
# a fetch may not be aimed inside the network fossick is running in
for _bad in ('http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/',   # cloud metadata
             'http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin', 'http://localhost/x', 'http://10.0.0.5/x',
             'http://192.168.1.1/', 'http://[::1]/', 'http://metadata.google.internal/',
             'http://0.0.0.0/', 'file:///etc/passwd'):
    try: check_url(_bad); raise SystemExit(f'not blocked: {_bad}')
    except BlockedURL: pass

assert check_url('https://example.com/a') == 'https://example.com/a'
assert check_url('http://127.0.0.1:8000/x', allow_private=True)     # the escape hatch is per-call

# the message has to name the way out, or the guard just gets deleted
try: check_url('http://localhost/x')
except BlockedURL as e: assert 'allow_private' in str(e) and 'FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE' in str(e)

# and the env var turns it off process-wide
os.environ['FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE'] = '1'
try: assert check_url('http://127.0.0.1/x')
finally: del os.environ['FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE']
```
